steps.text: Two large numbers are written in different notations. Which one is bigger?
Tap the correct sign — “<”, “=”, or “>” — for the comparison.
Then tap the highlighted check button to confirm.
Line up the place values: more digits means a bigger number; if the digit count is equal, compare from the left.

coach.mission: Compare the two numbers with <, =, or >.
whenStuck: Tap the correct sign, then “Check Sign”.
More digits usually means a bigger number.
whenWrong: Line up place values: more digits = bigger; if the digit count is equal, compare from the leftmost digit.
Convert both to the same notation first, then compare.
whenCorrect: You lined up the place values well.
coach.done: You can compare large numbers across notations. Keep going, or move on.

steps.text: Line up place values — more digits (or a bigger leading digit) is larger. Tap “<”, “=” or “>”.
Tap the highlighted check button to lock in your answer.

onCorrect: Correct comparison — place values lined up.
Yes! More digits means a bigger number.
onWrong: Count digits first: more digits = bigger. If equal, compare from the leftmost digit.
Convert both to the same notation, then compare place by place.
practice.done: You can compare large numbers across different notations!
